findings.what: The ?REFERENCE bullet now gives a false 'so', and its 'would be rEFERENCE' prediction contradicts the observation the same paragraph cites.
findings.why: Line 72 says 'A key the client sent keeps the rest of its casing, so an unknown query key that differs from a route parameter only in case (?REFERENCE=x) is a 400'. Casing does not cause the 400. RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:13-17 treats only Query-bound parameters as known, and the route-bound reference never is. Lower-case ?reference=X gives the same 400 (RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:84-95). The general rule 'keeps the rest of its casing' is contradicted by the only evidence for an upper-case key, docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217, saw 'reference'. The 'rEFERENCE' prediction at :74 reads ValidationProblems.cs:25-26 alone. It skips the step where the filter's AddModelError (:25) writes the key into ModelState, whose key handling the repo neither documents nor tests. David cannot defend either sentence (CLAUDE.md: every line explainable). This is the third round on this bullet (A2 R1, I1, I2). Fix direction, per I1 and inv-003 rec 3: keep what is proven. Body and model error keys get the first letter of each segment lower-cased (ValidationProblems.cs:25-26). Any unknown query key is a 400, including one that differs only in case from a route parameter (filter :13-17; pinned for lower case only). The ?REFERENCE key was seen once by hand as 'reference' and is not pinned. Drop the 'so' and the rEFERENCE prediction.
